pattern: Fast-moving location data plus a scarce resource: keep ephemeral positions in a sharded in-memory geo index (latest write wins), guard the scarce resource with short leases and a conditional write, and hand money off through an outbox and idempotency keys.

tips.nudge: What is the one thing a rider comes to the app to do?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for requesting a ride and getting a driver assigned.
tips.show: F2: A rider requests a ride (pickup, drop-off) and the system matches a nearby available driver who accepts.

tips.nudge: Before requesting, what does the rider see on the map?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for showing drivers around the rider.
tips.show: F1: Riders see nearby available drivers on a map with an ETA.

tips.nudge: Where does the system learn where drivers are?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for drivers reporting their position and riders tracking it.
tips.show: F3: Drivers send GPS location every ~4 s; riders track the assigned driver live.

tips.nudge: Two riders, one nearby driver, same second. What must never happen?
tips.hint: State a non-functional requirement about how many rides a driver can hold.
tips.show: N3: A driver is never assigned to two rides at once, and a ride never gets two drivers.

tips.nudge: How old can a driver's position be, and how fast must search answer?
tips.hint: Add non-functional targets for search latency and location freshness.
tips.show: N1/N2: positions at most a few seconds old; nearby search p99 < 100 ms; offer within ~5 s.

tips.nudge: How many drivers are online, and how often does each one report?
tips.hint: location updates/s = online drivers / seconds between updates.
tips.show: location_update_qps = 1M online drivers / 4 s ≈ 250,000 /s.

tips.nudge: Start from the number of trips per day.
tips.hint: ride requests/s = trips per day / 86,400 s; multiply for peak.
tips.show: ride_request_qps = 20M / day ≈ 230 /s (peak ×3 ≈ 700 /s): tiny next to location updates.

checks.label: Size of the live position set estimated

tips.nudge: If you kept every online driver's latest position, how much would it take?
tips.hint: memory = online drivers × bytes per entry (id, lat, lng, timestamp ≈ 100 B).
tips.show: geo_index_memory = 1M × 100 B ≈ 100 MB: it fits in RAM, so update rate, not size, is the problem.

tips.nudge: Which call starts the whole flow?
tips.hint: A POST that creates a ride with pickup and drop-off.
tips.show: POST /rides {pickup, dropoff, payment_method} + Idempotency-Key → 201 {ride_id, status: matching}

tips.nudge: How does the driver app send its position?
tips.hint: Define the call (or WebSocket message) the driver sends every few seconds.
tips.show: POST /drivers/location {lat, lng, heading, ts} over a persistent WebSocket → 204

tips.nudge: What record lives from request to payment?
tips.hint: One entity per ride with its status and the assigned driver.
tips.show: rides(ride_id PK, city, rider_id, driver_id, pickup, dropoff, status, fare, timestamps) in SQL sharded by city.

tips.nudge: Where is the latest driver position stored, keyed how?
tips.hint: An entity for the latest position per driver, organised for spatial lookup.
tips.show: driver_locations: city → GEO set of driver_id → (lat, lng) (geohash score), in Redis; overwritten every 4 s.

checks.label: Location ingestion designed as its own part

tips.nudge: 250k small writes per second that are stale in 4 s. Does that belong in your transactional store?
tips.hint: Add a part for ingesting driver updates: compare writing to SQL, buffering in Kafka and overwriting an in-memory index.
tips.show: Part 'Driver location ingestion': a location service overwrites the latest position in Redis GEO (sharded by city) and appends to a Kafka stream for live tracking.

checks.label: Spatial search designed as its own part

tips.nudge: A B-tree indexes one dimension. How do you search two?
tips.hint: Add a part for finding drivers near a point: compare lat/lng SQL ranges, geohash, quadtree and H3/S2.
tips.show: Part 'Nearby-driver search': geohash cells in Redis GEO per city; GEOSEARCH a radius and expand the ring if too few drivers.

checks.label: Assignment consistency designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Two matchers pick the same closest driver in the same millisecond. Who wins, and how?
tips.hint: Add a part for dispatch: compare broadcast-first-wins, DB row locks, a per-driver lease and a single dispatcher per city.
tips.show: Part 'Matching and dispatch': lease the driver with SET NX PX 15000, offer once, and accept only if the lease still names this ride, via a conditional UPDATE … WHERE status='matching' plus a unique index on the driver's active ride.

checks.label: Trip lifecycle and payment designed as its own part

tips.nudge: The trip ends; the card must be charged once. What if the payment provider times out?
tips.hint: Add a part for the trip state machine and how completion hands off to payments.
tips.show: Part 'Trip state and payments handoff': commit the transition plus an outbox event; a worker charges the PSP with Idempotency-Key = ride_id.

checks.label: Nearby search keeps up with constant position changes

tips.nudge: Where do the ~1M latest positions live so a search takes milliseconds?
tips.hint: Add an in-memory store that holds driver positions.
tips.show: Redis GEO (or an in-memory quadtree/H3 index) holding the latest driver positions, sharded by city.

tips.nudge: Millions of phones hold connections open. What spreads them?
tips.hint: Put something in front of stateless service instances.
tips.show: Rider and driver apps → API gateway / load balancer (HTTPS + WebSocket) → service instances.

checks.label: Location updates feed other consumers without blocking ingestion

tips.nudge: Live tracking and trip history both need positions. Should the location service call them directly?
tips.hint: Have the location service publish to an asynchronous log that other components consume.
tips.show: Location service → location stream (Kafka) → push gateway (live tracking) and trip-route archiving.

checks.label: Partitioning of the hot data decided

tips.nudge: One Redis key for every driver on Earth: what breaks first?
tips.hint: Decide how the geo index and dispatch are partitioned, and what happens at the borders.
tips.show: Shard by city (rides are local); split megacities by geohash prefix; search neighbouring shards near borders.

tips.nudge: Which component sees the most load, and in which cities?
tips.hint: Walk the location path and the dispatch path and name what saturates first.
tips.show: Location ingestion in megacities (shard by city + geohash prefix), per-city matching, and the WebSocket push gateway's connection count.

tips.nudge: A geo shard dies, the PSP times out, a driver loses signal mid-offer. What happens?
tips.hint: Name each failure and how the design recovers.
tips.show: Geo shard: replica + positions refill within 4 s. PSP down: retry from Kafka with the same idempotency key. Lost driver: lease TTL frees the ride.
